title: A Mars Rover Just Broke the Distance Record
description: On 11 October 2026 NASA's Perseverance passed Opportunity's off-world driving record of about 45.16 km, reaching about 45.22 km. IEEE Spectrum credits its AutoNav self-driving software, used for roughly nine tenths of its driving.

beats.text: Mars has a new distance champion
beats.vo: A robot on Mars just broke the record for driving farthest on another world.

points: Autonomy drives most of the way
beats.vo: On eleven October, N A S A's Perseverance passed Opportunity's record of about forty-five kilometres. I E E E Spectrum credits its self-driving software, which handles around nine tenths of its driving. Humans still set the long-range route and mark areas to avoid, like sand.
Follow for a daily dose of engineering.

caption:
A Mars rover just took the off-world driving record. 🔴
On 11 Oct 2026 NASA's Perseverance passed Opportunity's ~45.16 km, reaching ~45.22 km. IEEE Spectrum credits AutoNav self-driving for most of it — but humans still plan routes and mark no-go sand.
Why care: autonomy is what makes distance possible when radio delay rules out a joystick.
